title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1968-06-14
lineage: AUD > MC > R > R > PCM > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: A lo‑fi audience tape that still captures the incendiary Fillmore East debut, highlighted by a monster 24‑minute “Caution” and wild feedback sandwich.
ai_review.review: This AUD recording is far from pristine – drums and vocals are often buried, the mix is oversaturated and at times muddy – but the performance shines through. The show is legendary for its opening and closing feedback blasts, the blistering 24‑minute "Caution", and a rare Space → The Eleven → St. Stephen sequence that fans describe as pure primal energy. For anyone chasing the most extreme 1968 Dead experience, the music outweighs the technical flaws.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews praise the show’s historic intensity and standout performances (high show weight), while consistently noting poor to fair audio quality (low recording weight). Weighted average yields a solid but not stellar rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Oversaturated, muddy AUD tape; drums and vocals often inaudible, Phil’s bass faint, but Jerry’s guitar cuts through. Some reviewers call it "atrocious" while others say it’s decent for a 1968 audience recording.

poor_songs: "Lovelight" (mentioned as less exceptional by one reviewer)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set opens with a wall of feedback, moves through chaotic psychedelic jams, and closes with another feedback burst – a true "feedback sandwich" that frames the wild improvisations.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Consistently audible; described as “unconscious” on guitar, tone loud and dominant throughout the tape.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for powerful "bombs" despite being barely audible in the mix.
band_member_comments.Bob: Drums largely buried; mentioned as “almost inaudible” but still part of the primal wall of sound.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill & Kreutzmann’s playing is difficult to hear, yet reviewers note the overall percussive intensity.
